title: Shared git repository and counting stand-in test fixtures
description:
Give tests one way to build a git repository through the git CLI and one counting stand-in for the git executable.

## Background

- `test_add_pinned_document_uses_pinned_document_and_asset_bytes` (`crates/jit/tests/fast_docs_templates/document_event_log_tests.rs:253`) builds its commit through libgit2 (`git2::Repository::init` at `:259`, `git2::Signature` at `:272`), reaching the crate's normal `git2` dependency.
- Two counting wrappers exist: `counted_git` (`crates/jit/tests/fast_docs_templates/git_revision_tests.rs:166-181`) and `capture_git_fixture` (`crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store_tests.rs:2585-2632`). Each writes a `#!/bin/sh` script that logs `$*` and runs `exec git "$@"`. Placed first on `PATH` under the name `git`, such a script would run itself, so a stand-in for the executable must run the real git by absolute path.
- Shared test helpers live in the library's test-support surface, `jit::test_harness` (`crates/jit/src/test_harness.rs`), compiled under `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))` (`crates/jit/src/lib.rs:36`). The crate's own tests and every integration suite enable `test-support`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `jit::test_harness` offers a git repository fixture that initializes a repository through the git CLI with a repository-local user name and email, writes files, and commits them, returning the new commit's id.
- [hard] REQ-02: `jit::test_harness` offers, on Unix, a counting stand-in for the git executable: a file named `git` in its own directory that records each invocation's arguments and then runs the real git, resolved to an absolute path when the stand-in is created. Each recorded invocation exposes its arguments with a leading `-C <dir>` pair removed, since the git module starts every process that way. A test can read the recorded invocations, pass the stand-in as an explicit program, or put its directory first on a child process's `PATH`.
- [hard] REQ-03: Fixture tests show that the stand-in records each invocation's arguments in order, with and without a leading `-C <dir>` pair, and returns the real git's output and exit status, and that the repository fixture's commit id is the repository's `HEAD`.

## Notes

- The stand-in is `#[cfg(unix)]`, as both existing wrappers are.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

title: Storage-owned git module with a one-process probe
description:
Create the storage-owned module that is the only place jit starts git, with the one-process probe that classifies a directory.

## Background

- Ten production files start git today, each naming the literal `git`, among them layout detection (`crates/jit/src/storage/worktree_paths.rs:58-141`), claims, worktree commands, validation, init and gate execution. Charter decision `@/charter/D-21` gives git one storage-owned module that runs the CLI.
- `git -C <dir> rev-parse --git-common-dir --show-toplevel` answers both layout facts in one process. It succeeds in a primary checkout, a linked checkout and a repository without commits, and exits nonzero outside a repository and inside a `.git` directory. A relative common directory is resolved against the probed directory, as `:104-109` does today. A failure to start git means no executable is available.
- No production setting names a git executable. `JsonFileStorage.git_program` (`crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:403`) defaults to `git` (`:441`) and only a `#[cfg(test)]` constructor changes it (`crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:481-488`).
- `WorktreePaths` (`crates/jit/src/storage/worktree_paths.rs:13`) is the layout value the CLI detects once (`crates/jit/src/main.rs:1903`) and hands to storage, the executor, claims and worktree commands; `is_git_repository()` (`crates/jit/src/storage/worktree_paths.rs:144`) says whether it is a git checkout.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `crates/jit/src/storage/git.rs` (`storage::git`, public) holds a `Git` value naming the git executable, whose default is the bare name `git` looked up on `PATH`, and `Git::with_program` names another. Every process the module starts runs as `<program> -C <directory> …`, never in the process working directory, and a failure to start one is the module error for an unavailable executable, naming the program.
- [hard] REQ-02: `GitCheckout` pairs a `Git` with a checkout's worktree root and carries the module's git operations. `WorktreePaths::git()` returns one for a git checkout, built with the default executable, and `None` otherwise.
- [hard] REQ-03: `Git::probe(dir)` classifies a directory with one git process. A primary checkout, a linked checkout and a repository without commits yield the common directory and the top-level path; a directory outside a repository, a `.git` directory, and an executable that cannot start yield no checkout.
- [hard] REQ-04: The module's behaviour suite, a new module of the `fast_docs_templates` suite, proves REQ-03 against real repositories and counts one process per probe with the shared counting stand-in.

## Notes

- The module gains one operation for each git fact production code needs, each just before its first production consumer; in the end state every public item has a production caller. Without an executable, core commands behave as outside git (`@/charter/D-4`).
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

title: Layout consumers share invocation-owned checkout facts
description:
Keep Git layout observations in one invocation-owned context so bootstrap and checkout projections reuse facts instead of probing a checkout again.

## Background

`WorktreePaths::detect_from_with_non_git_root` (`crates/jit/src/storage/worktree_paths.rs:84`) probes the selected data root, then the explicit worktree root when the data root is external. `for_worktree_root` (`:204`) currently probes the selected checkout again and probes a sibling each time it is projected. The external-store investigation measured four layout processes for a two-checkout listing and for active-lease validation.

The reconciled layout contract permits one computation per distinct checkout context: ordinary issue reads use at most one Git process, external bootstrap uses at most two layout processes, and an external-store operation visiting N distinct checkout contexts including the selected checkout uses at most N+1 layout processes. The failed data-root probe is included; lease and issue counts cannot increase this bound. Existing external-store coordination and per-checkout identity behavior remain required.

`JsonFileStorage::configured_worktree_paths` (`crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:612`) and `CommandExecutor::require_worktree_paths` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2589`) still discover layouts when callers omit them. The shared bootstrap already supplies paths to both handles. Recovery's nested repair executor (`crates/jit/src/commands/claim.rs`, `ClaimOps::recover`) can receive the existing paths while retaining the fallible `with_layout` binding introduced on main.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Detection retains each queried path's successful, absent, or error outcome in one invocation-scoped layout context. A successful probe associates only the queried path, its filesystem-canonical alias when available, and the Git-reported top level with that checkout. Bootstrap preserves data-root-first selection and the external fallback, with at most one layout process for an in-checkout data root and at most two for an external data root. Negative observations are not broadened to parent or descendant paths; common and private Git directories are not treated as equivalent worktree probe paths.
- [hard] REQ-02: Cloning and projecting supplied worktree paths retain the same context. `for_worktree_root` reuses the selected checkout and previously observed siblings, including absent siblings, without another probe; concurrent identical requests cannot duplicate a process. An external operation visiting N distinct checkout contexts including the selected checkout uses at most N+1 layout processes regardless of repeated listed paths or lease count. Data-root ownership, linked-store write policy, common-directory coordination, subdirectory roots, separate identities, and moved or previously unvisited checkout behavior remain unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: Storage and executor no longer call a layout detector when paths are absent. Unconfigured storage reads only its local data root; an unconfigured executor reports non-Git paths from its explicit layout or existing storage-root fallback and takes no lease guard. Production bootstrap and recovery construction share supplied context, preserve fallible layout binding and recovery ordering, and keep missing Git optional for core commands. Existing primary-tier fixtures supply their paths explicitly.
- [hard] REQ-04: The worktree-path mechanism tests own exact-alias, negative/error reuse, clone sharing, and concurrent duplicate-probe behavior. The existing CLI process-budget suite covers external primary/linked bootstrap and external worktree listing plus active-lease validation, including a selected subdirectory and moved sibling, and checks the revised bounds without growth from additional leases. Existing ordinary-read process assertions and external-store identity/coordination tests remain passing; no duplicate behavioral matrix or new Cargo test target is introduced.

## Notes

The implementation follows the reconciled `layout-once` contract and proposed DEC-27. The historical evidence is `dev/active/f4d9502a-git-cli-module/layout-probe-investigation.md`. Git remains the classifier; no new authority flag, Git-file parser, persistent cache, or inferred sibling administrative path is introduced. Layout value equality remains independent of mutable observation state. The distinct roles of `git()`, `write_checkout()`, and the guarded initialization-identity path remain intact.

planning.outcome: Bootstrap and checkout projections reuse invocation-owned layout facts within the distinct-context process bounds.

title: One head lookup in the git module
description:
Add the module's single lookup of the checked-out commit and branch, so every consumer of either fact asks one bounded operation backed by at most two git processes.

## Background

Six branch lookups exist, with differing semantics:

| Site | Command | Detached HEAD | Unborn branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| `crates/jit/src/commands/claim.rs:46-64` | `rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` | `HEAD` | second process, then a typed no-commits error |
| `crates/jit/src/commands/worktree.rs:46-63` | same | `HEAD` | generic error |
| `crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs:974-993` | same | `HEAD` | error, read as no branch |
| `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:3350` | `branch --show-current` | empty string | the unborn branch's name |
| `crates/jit/src/gate_execution.rs:551`, `crates/jit/src/gate_execution.rs:567` | `rev-parse HEAD`, `rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` | `HEAD` | none |
| `crates/jit/src/commands/snapshot.rs:25-29` | libgit2 `head().shorthand()` | `HEAD` | none |

A previously recognized checkout can become invalid, so a nonzero exit cannot establish an unborn branch. Read HEAD identity with `rev-parse --revs-only HEAD --symbolic-full-name HEAD`, then validate the captured OID with `rev-list --no-walk --missing=print <oid> --`, or validate a successful empty identity result with `symbolic-ref --quiet HEAD`. Both processes use `--no-replace-objects`; commit validation also uses child-local `-c core.commitGraph=false`. The domain's commit identity is `CanonicalCommitOid`. [The approved experiment](dev/active/f4d9502a-git-cli-module/head-lookup-experiment.md) records the protocol and failure evidence.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `GitCheckout::head()` starts at most two configured git processes, reading only HEAD identity and its captured commit or validating the unborn symbolic target, with no unrelated ref, reflog, ancestor or worktree traversal and no lazy fetch. It returns `Ok(None)` only on a confirmed unborn branch, and otherwise a `Head` holding the commit as `CanonicalCommitOid` and the branch name, absent on a detached HEAD.
- [hard] REQ-02: `Head` renders its branch as the branch name, or `HEAD` when detached, which is what `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` prints.
- [hard] REQ-03: An executable that cannot start returns the module's unavailable error. Only a successfully validated unborn branch returns `Ok(None)`; command failures, missing, corrupt or non-commit objects, and malformed output return typed errors, including after a previously recognized checkout becomes invalid.
- [hard] REQ-04: The owning behavior suite covers branch, detached, unborn, missing executable, stale or invalid checkout, malformed refs, missing or corrupt commit and non-commit objects, and bounds each lookup at two processes. Focused regressions prove no promisor fetch or unrelated history/worktree traversal, and rejection of missing objects masked by commit graphs or replacements.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
